source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Enter BMC Web UI and navigate to the Network protocol properties page.
2. Check text displayed and make sure it is readable.
3. Enable DNS and fill out the information for the DNS server.
These changes should be made for both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.
4. Save / Apply changes and wait 3 to 5 minutes.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. DNS information should be displayed correctly.
2. All displayed text must be readable.
3. All steps must be completed with all supported browsers.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" lan print 1 2>&1 | grep -iE "IP Address|MAC"; echo ---dns-set---; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" lan set 1 dns1 8.8.8.8 2>&1; echo ---lan-print-dns---; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" lan print 1 2>&1 | grep -i "dns"
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return `ipmitool lan print` IP/MAC/DNS lines after setting the DNS server, so the user confirms DNS is displayed and configured for IPv4 (IPv6 DNS + Web UI text readability still checked by operator in the GUI).
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: sets the BMC DNS server (write to network config) and validates IPv4 path; IPv6 DNS and the Web UI text/readability part of the criteria are operator-side GUI checks.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL admits its IPv4-only limitation but still proposes a public resolver, assumed channel/cipher, plaintext credential argument and an IPMI `dns1` operation whose support is not established. It cannot cover IPv6 or browser readability.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly restores IPv4, IPv6, browser-matrix and rollback coverage. This review retains the classification while separating source-required display/readability from optional functional resolver probes.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 827/2291 repeats the incomplete command and labels it conditional without checking dual-stack completeness, public-DNS policy, UI/browser evidence or restore behavior.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Its non-counting sequence-991 draft was inspected only as history. It under-classified the hybrid case as MANUAL ONLY even though configuration readback, persistence and resolver probes are material automatable evidence.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-35 preserves the dual-stack writable setting workflow instead of reducing it to read-only; ED-36 treats resolver and browser matrices as readiness inputs; ED-38 keeps the configuration change and verdict engineer-owned.

original_test_intent: Verify through every Project-supported browser that the BMC WebUI DNS controls and text are readable and correctly display saved IPv4 and IPv6 DNS information after enable/apply and the specified three-to-five-minute stabilization interval.
original_method: For each approved browser/version, an operator navigates the BMC Network Protocol Properties page, inspects labels/text, enables DNS, enters approved IPv4 and IPv6 resolver values, applies them, waits three to five minutes and verifies the displayed/persisted information. Protected readback and resolver probes may provide supporting evidence but do not replace browser presentation checks.
manual_activity: A qualified operator approves the DNS write, confirms the browser-support matrix and visually judges text readability/correct display in every selected browser. Automation may drive an approved UI/API path and collect dual-stack readback, persistence, optional resolution and screenshots, but the engineer owns visual acceptance and recovery.
required_inputs: Immutable chassis/BMC/firmware/interface/channel identity and authoritative DNS fields, supported address syntax and apply behavior
Owner-approved reachable IPv4 and IPv6 resolver addresses plus any required domain/search fields; public resolvers are permitted only if the Project network policy explicitly approves them
Supported browser names, exact versions, client OS, UI language, zoom/DPI/viewport and definition of readable/correct text
Expected WebUI labels, enable state and normalized IPv4/IPv6 display values before save, after three-to-five minutes and after reload or new login
Prior DNS configuration, protected credential mechanism, maintenance approval, alternate address-based access, restore order and optional Project-approved query targets
safety_requirements: Do not use `8.8.8.8`, another public resolver or guessed IPv6 values unless explicitly approved for the isolated management network; DNS writes can redirect or break name-based services.
Verify the exact BMC and supported configuration path before writing. Do not assume IPMI channel 1, cipher 17 or `lan set ... dns1` is implemented by the target firmware.
Use protected credentials rather than `-P` with a logged password and preserve alternate access by literal IP/local console in case name resolution or UI sessions fail.
Exercise both IPv4 and IPv6 fields independently and do not credit an IPv4-only result as dual-stack coverage. Record rejected/unsupported field behavior rather than guessing syntax.
Run the complete apply/wait/reload sequence for each supported browser selected by Project SPEC; a screenshot from one browser cannot cover the rest.
Do not clear unrelated production logs merely because the template says clear logs. Snapshot and filter relevant BMC/network/audit records according to retention policy.

Do not automatically retry saves. Stop on wrong resolver/target, BMC loss, malformed display, unexpected service impact, credential exposure or failed restore; use alternate access and restore the exact prior values.
agent_execution_scope: Before approval, validate browser matrix, BMC field semantics, dual-stack resolver reachability, exact write/readback method and rollback without changing DUT state.
After approval, collect per-browser before/after screenshots or DOM evidence, timestamps, dual-stack configuration readback and optional bounded queries to Project-owned test names.
Treat UI readability/display, stored values and functional resolution as distinct evidence; functional queries are supporting checks unless Project SPEC explicitly adds them to acceptance.
Do not select resolver values, make an unapproved change, infer visual readability solely from IPMI output, retry automatically or issue DUT PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the resolver values, supported-browser matrix, UI readability standard, change window, alternate access and restore plan.
Observe or attest the WebUI text/display and save workflow in each browser and intervene if management access is affected.
Restore the original DNS configuration, verify final access and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its readback concept is useful only as supporting evidence. The literal method is rejected because it writes an unapproved public IPv4 resolver, omits IPv6 and all browser/UI checkpoints, assumes unsupported channel/cipher/command semantics and exposes the password.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the platform-approved WebUI/API or validated management command with protected credentials to set the approved IPv4 and IPv6 fields. Collect per-browser UI evidence plus authoritative readback; run Project-owned resolver queries only as separately identified functional support.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: WebUI Network Protocol page, readability, IPv4 plus IPv6 changes, Save/Apply, three-to-five-minute wait, every supported browser, no Script and 10/10-minute estimates remain unmodified.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Snapshot prior DNS; execute the enable/set/apply/wait/reload flow for each approved browser using the same IPv4/IPv6 matrix; compare displayed and persisted fields; optionally prove resolver reachability with controlled names; restore and verify the original configuration.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact BMC WebUI/firmware and Project-approved dual-stack management network/browser matrix.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware, browser/OS, automation driver if used, resolver and management-client versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform BMC DNS field specification, Project resolver policy and browser support matrix.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact dual-stack values, per-browser environment identity, authoritative persistence/readback, protected access and reversible recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: IPMI readback cannot prove WebUI text readability; one browser cannot cover the matrix; IPv4-only configuration cannot prove IPv6 fields; successful DNS queries do not by themselves prove correct UI display.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Dual-stack resolver plan, UI/browser matrix, write method, stabilization, recovery and approval.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Incorrect resolvers can disrupt name-based BMC features, and visual rendering defects may be browser/version/locale-specific even when stored values are correct.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC defines the finite supported-browser matrix and approved resolver values. Any API-only execution must record that WebUI display/readability remains unverified rather than claiming equivalent full coverage.
expected_evidence: BMC/firmware/interface identity, approved IPv4/IPv6 DNS plan, prior state and browser/version/OS/language/viewport matrix
For every supported browser: Network Protocol page before/after evidence showing readable labels, enable state and exact IPv4/IPv6 values
Save/apply timestamps, three-to-five-minute stabilization, reload/new-session persistence and authoritative protected readback
Optional Project-owned A/AAAA or other approved resolver query evidence clearly labeled as functional support rather than a substitute for UI acceptance
Restored prior DNS values, stable address-based and name-based access, relevant BMC/audit/network logs and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and Criteria consistently require dual-stack DNS configuration and cross-browser WebUI presentation. The unspecified resolver values and supported-browser list are Project execution inputs, not contradictions.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The workflow and acceptance surfaces are clear. Resolver values, browser matrix, UI expectations and recovery are supplyable readiness inputs, so missing data does not permanently block the review.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects its unsafe IPv4-only/public-resolver shortcut and restores IPv6 plus browser/UI coverage.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on package/user confirmation while more carefully distinguishing source-required presentation from additional functional resolution evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces command-presence reasoning with a dual-stack, per-browser and reversible evidence matrix.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Changes MANUAL ONLY to package/user confirmation because automated persistence/readback and controlled resolver checks are material, while keeping visual verdict ownership manual.

review_improvement: Prevents one IPv4 write and filtered CLI output from falsely passing a dual-stack, all-supported-browser UI test, and prevents unapproved public DNS from entering the management network.
independent_technical_reasoning: The source combines a writable dual-stack configuration workflow with visual compatibility acceptance. Neither half subsumes the other: stored values and optional queries can be automated, while human-approved UI readability across the actual browser matrix remains a separate checkpoint. That mixed evidence model is package/user confirmation, not manual-only and not blocked.
